title: [ORION-QG QG-14] Compositional regime calculus: combine compiler optimality certificates across quantum subroutines
body:
Parent programme: #740
Founding theorem/forecast objects: QG-6, QG-8, QG-10, QG-12
FT composition context: QG-11 #764

## Status

**COMPOSITION FRONTIER — compose proof-carrying regime/normal-form summaries, not merely compiler passes.**

Real quantum algorithms combine multiple compilation subproblems: PREP/SELECT, block encodings, QSVT/polynomial sequences, arithmetic/oracles, routing, QEC/logical operations, measurement/feed-forward. ORION-QG currently proves regime geometry mostly one family at a time.

QG-14 asks:

> When can independently certified compiler regime geometries be composed to infer the globally preferred normal forms/cost bounds without reopening each component's internal optimizer, and exactly what cross-component couplings invalidate that composition?

## Strong donor subtraction

Compositional compilation is established:
- **qstack** (2026) provides compositional end-to-end FT quantum compilation through quantum/QEC/ISA layers and wraps classical callbacks;
- modular/verified compilation and direct refinements between open modules are established PL theory;
- modular quantum uncomputation/synthesis, modular compiler IRs, ScaffCC-style scalable modular compilation and current QRE pipelines are prior art.

Therefore QG-14 cannot claim novelty for compiler-pass composition, modular IRs, semantic refinement, or modular resource estimation.

Candidate contribution is only a **calculus for composing ORION-QG optimality/regime certificates**: normal-form families, parameter cells, interval bounds, obstruction certificates and explicit unresolved couplings.

## Component certificate

A component i exports a proof-carrying interface:

```text
RegimeInterface
semantic_input_contract
semantic_output_contract
admitted_information/access
resource_coordinates
objective_parameters
certified_region K_i
normal_form_family F_i
cost_expression / interval
boundary_predicates
certificate_obligations
latent_coupling_coordinates
CANNOT_CHECK_conditions
provenance/backend/compiler identity
```

The internal optimizer need not be exposed if the interface theorem is sufficient.

## C1 — separable composition theorem

For independent components with additive resources

`r_total = sum_i r_i`

and no shared constraints except typed semantic composition, prove:

- if each component theorem is applicable under the same global objective projection;
- each selected normal form is independently optimal for its component;
- component choices do not change another component's feasible set/resource map;

then the tuple of component-optimal normal forms is globally optimal for the product family and total cost is the sum of certified component costs.

This is elementary separable optimization and receives zero novelty credit; the scientific value is the machine-checked compiler interface and anti-coupling conditions.

## C2 — shared-budget composition

If components share a global budget/resource (ancilla pool, T factories, error budget, routing fabric, measurement channel), independent optimality may fail.

Represent coupling by explicit coordinates/constraints:

`H(r_1,...,r_m) <= 0`.

Possible certified strategies:
- Lagrange/dual prices convert shared constraints to component objective coefficients and use QG-8/QG-11 phase cells;
- finite budget allocation DP over component regime summaries;
- interval bounds from QG-10 where exact allocation is unavailable.

Any duality/DP mathematics is donor-owned. QG-14 must preserve exact conditions under which the composed certificate is valid.

## C3 — regime-boundary convolution

For components with piecewise-linear/polyhedral cost envelopes, compute the global parameter-space arrangement induced by all component boundaries plus shared-budget constraints.

Output cells contain:
- selected normal-form tuple;
- exact/interval total resource expression;
- active component boundary predicates;
- coupling certificate;
- distance/margin to nearest regime change.

The number of Cartesian cells may explode; exploit certificate arity/low-order obstruction structure where proven, but do not assume it generically.

## C4 — cross-component counterexample hunt

Actively construct cases where independently valid local regimes fail globally because of a hidden coupling:

- two components individually choose T-heavy low-qubit forms but jointly saturate magic-state factories;
- separate ancilla-minimal forms serialize a shared measurement bottleneck;
- local PREP/SELECT choices change global QSVT normalization/query count;
- block-encoding scaling changes the number/degree of later polynomial transforms;
- shared routing/layout causes a local support reduction to increase total communication;
- error-budget allocation changes code distances differently across components.

A minimal witness is a positive scientific result:

`QG14_LOCAL_REGIME_CERTIFICATES_NOT_COMPOSITIONALLY_SUFFICIENT__MISSING_COUPLING_<id>`.

It identifies a coordinate that must be added to RegimeInterface.

## C5 — first exact compositional calibration

Build a synthetic/exact two-component world from already solved ORION-QG families:

- component A: R6M TARE/QG-8 objective-phase theorem;
- component B: SixLCU/QG-12 theorem or a second R6M instance;
- first arm strictly additive -> separable theorem must predict exact product optimum;
- second arm introduce one frozen shared resource coupling -> naive product must fail and coupling-aware calculus must recover exact optimum.

Use exact enumeration/DP as hidden referee only after composed prediction is frozen.

## C6 — real algorithmic vertical slice

After exact calibration, choose an actual algorithmic pipeline with at least two materially coupled compilation components, e.g.:
- LCU block encoding + qubitization/QSVT;
- PREP/SELECT + amplitude-amplification/query layer;
- Hamiltonian block encoding + FT factory/layout layer.

Freeze donor implementations and interface contracts first. Compare:
- monolithic best-known compiler/QRE;
- independent component regime selection;
- QG-14 coupling-aware composition.

Claim only the exact earned layer (logical/FT estimate, not observed speedup).

## C7 — incremental recomposition

A practical benefit of certificate composition should be **local invalidation**: when one component/backend/objective changes, only downstream regime interfaces whose assumptions depend on it reopen. Recompute affected cells rather than the entire monolithic optimization.

Measure:
- proof/certificate reuse fraction;
- recomputation cost;
- false stale-certificate rate (must be zero);
- agreement with full recomputation on calibration worlds.

Dynamic assurance/dependency invalidation are prior art; candidate value is the concrete compiler-regime composition semantics.

## Dual harness

Generic ORION harness:
- independently reconstructs component certificate applicability and composed cost/bounds;
- runs hidden monolithic referee on calibration worlds only after prediction;
- verifies counterexamples/coupling witnesses.

Native ORION-Q harness:
- blocks composition when any latent coupling coordinate is unresolved;
- tracks which interface assumptions depend on which component/resource identity;
- performs scoped reopen on component/backend/objective changes.

## Positive terminals

- `QG14_SEPARABLE_REGIME_COMPOSITION_THEOREM_MACHINE_CHECKED`
- `QG14_COUPLING_AWARE_REGIME_COMPOSITION_SUPPORTED`
- `QG14_PROSPECTIVE_COMPOSED_REGIME_FORECAST_CONFIRMED`
- `QG14_LOCAL_CERTIFICATE_INSUFFICIENCY__NEW_COUPLING_COORDINATE_FOUND`
- `QG14_INCREMENTAL_RECOMPOSITION_VALUE_SUPPORTED`

Honest alternatives:
- `QG14_COMPOSITION_REQUIRES_MONOLITHIC_STATE__NO_COMPRESSION_VALUE`
- `QG14_DONOR_PARENT_FOUND`
- `QG14_CANNOT_CHECK`

## Novelty boundary

No claim to invent compositional compilation, modular verification, Lagrangian decomposition, dynamic programming, Pareto convolution or dependency invalidation. Candidate contribution is restricted to **proof-carrying composition of quantum compiler regime/optimality certificates with explicit coupling and reopen semantics**.
